ip_top_stories.title: China Issues Draft Regulations on AI Copyright Infringement
ip_top_stories.summary: China has released draft regulations specifically addressing copyright infringement in the context of AI. The move signals a significant step toward formal legislative frameworks governing AI-generated content and training data use in one of the world's largest AI markets.

ip_top_stories.title: Delhi HC Examines Copyright Eligibility of AI-Generated Art in Landmark DABUS Case
ip_top_stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed India's Copyright Office to decide within eight weeks whether AI-generated artwork can be registered under Indian copyright law, following a petition by a US researcher. The case has significant implications for how AI authorship is treated globally, with the court's scrutiny drawing parallels to international debates sparked by the DABUS AI inventor cases.

ip_top_stories.title: Cox v. Sony Music Comes to Hollywood
ip_top_stories.summary: The Cox v. Sony Music copyright liability case, which established significant precedent around internet service provider responsibility for user infringement, is now drawing attention from Hollywood stakeholders. The case's outcomes could shape how platform and ISP liability for AI-related copyright infringement is interpreted going forward.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic's Legal Overhang: Piracy Trial Could Unravel Ethical AI Premium
ip_top_stories.summary: Analysis of the ongoing copyright litigation against Anthropic warns that an adverse ruling in the training data piracy trial could undermine the company's market positioning as an ethically-oriented AI developer. The case centres on whether Anthropic's use of copyrighted material to train its Claude models constitutes infringement.

ip_top_stories.title: Tech's AI Coding Boom On Collision Course With Copyright
ip_top_stories.summary: The rapid expansion of AI coding tools is raising urgent copyright questions about the use of open-source and proprietary code in training datasets. Legal experts warn that unresolved questions around code copyright could expose major technology companies to significant liability.

ip_further_links.title: Another judge agrees: AI-Created art isn't copyrightable
ip_further_links.summary: A further US judicial ruling has confirmed that artwork generated solely by AI does not meet the human authorship requirement for copyright protection.

ip_further_links.title: Cox v Sony: Infringers gonna infringe – unless service providers encourage them
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat analyses the Cox v Sony Music ruling and its implications for secondary copyright liability of service providers whose users engage in infringement.

ip_further_links.title: AI Code Leak Exposes the Fault Lines of Copyright
ip_further_links.summary: A leaked AI codebase has reignited debate about the boundaries of copyright protection for software and training data used in AI development.

ip_further_links.title: AI And Human Authorship Requirement: Reflections From The US Position And Implications For Indian Copyright Law
ip_further_links.summary: Legal analysis examines how the US Copyright Office's human authorship requirement may influence the development of Indian copyright doctrine in relation to AI-generated works.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI Freezes UK Stargate Project: Energy Costs and Copyright Rules Delay 8,000-GPU Plan
ip_further_links.summary: OpenAI has paused its UK Stargate data centre project, with copyright regulatory uncertainty cited alongside energy costs as a contributing factor to the delay.

ip_further_links.title: Apple accused of copyright infringement over AI training on YouTube videos
ip_further_links.summary: Apple is facing accusations of copyright infringement for allegedly using YouTube videos without authorisation to train its AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: Fordham 33 (Report 2): Top 5 Takeaways: Data Governance, Privacy, & Cybersecurity in an AI World
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat reports on key takeaways from the Fordham IP Conference regarding data governance, privacy, and cybersecurity frameworks as they intersect with AI development.

ip_further_links.title: [Courting Controversy] Now You See Me, Now You Don't: The Illusion of Authorship
ip_further_links.summary: Legal commentary explores the philosophical and legal tensions around AI authorship claims and what it means for copyright doctrine when the creative agent is non-human.

ip_further_links.title: AI-Generated Animation: Implement Legal Regulations to Protect Copyright Holders
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary piece calls for specific legal regulations to address the copyright challenges posed by AI-generated animation and protect rights holders in the creative industries.

ip_further_links.title: Fordham 33 (Report 1): Government Leader's Perspective on IP
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat's first report from the Fordham IP Conference covers government leaders' perspectives on the evolving intellectual property landscape in the age of AI.
